Slowly: 3 s down and 3 s up, no pauses; don’t lock out at the top and don’t relax at the bottom — the muscle stays tense the whole time. How it is counted

A set counts in full for the exercise’s target group and as half a set for the other working groups — the same as the weekly chart in the plan (Pelland et al., 2026). Only logged sets count; “10 per side” is one set.

Target: 10–20 sets per muscle group per week — from 10 sets muscles grow noticeably more (Schoenfeld, Ogborn, Krieger, 2017).

Status comes from the last workout in which the group did 2 or more sets as a main mover: under 48 h ago — fatigued, 48–72 h — recovering, 72 h or more — ready. If you don’t take sets to your limit, muscles mostly recover in 24–48 h; after sets to your limit — in up to 72 h (Morán-Navarro et al., 2017). Work as a secondary muscle and cardio don’t change the status. The log stores dates only, so hours are counted in days: yesterday — 24 h, 2 days ago — 48 h, 3 days ago — 72 h.

Today’s workout: groups with the biggest shortfall to 10 sets come first (big muscles before small ones), fatigued groups are skipped, recovering groups get one exercise with one set fewer. Gear, level and number of exercises come from the plan settings.
